outputs.L2: The disclosed technology concerns a vehicle laser illumination apparatus having at least two laser emitters. The secondary beams are aimed by microscanners at a light-converting element, where they form a predetermined luminous pattern. The invention relates to a laser lighting device intended for use in vehicles. The device comprises at least two laser light sources, each configured to generate a primary laser light beam having a first intensity profile. Each primary laser light beam is coupled into an associated light guide, which modifies the beam as it propagates through the guide. The beam then exits the light guide as a secondary laser light beam having an intensity profile that differs from the first intensity profile.

Each secondary laser light beam is directed by a corresponding microscanner onto a light conversion means. The microscanners control the paths of the secondary beams across the light conversion means so as to generate a predefined luminous image. A projection system then projects this luminous image from the light conversion means onto the roadway, thereby producing a desired vehicle illumination pattern.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a laser-lighting device for a vehicle, particularly a lighting device configured to project a predefined light distribution or image onto a roadway. The device comprises a plurality of laser-light sources, each of which emits a primary laser beam. Each laser-light source is optically coupled to a corresponding light guide, so that the primary laser beams can be guided and conditioned independently of one another.

The individual light guides are configured to modify the intensity profiles of the respective primary laser beams. In particular, a light guide may redistribute, homogenize, shape, or otherwise transform the intensity of the associated beam across its cross section. This optical conditioning makes it possible to provide each beam with an intensity distribution suitable for subsequent scanning and image formation. Because the beams are processed through separate light guides, their intensity profiles may be adapted individually to the desired contribution of each laser-light source.

After leaving the light guides, the conditioned primary laser beams are directed toward one or more microscanners. Each microscanner can deflect its associated beam in at least one scanning direction and may, for example, include a micromechanical mirror capable of pivoting about one or two axes. By controlling the microscanners over time, the primary laser beams are scanned across selected regions of a light-conversion element. The scanning paths, dwell times, and beam intensities can be coordinated to generate a desired spatial intensity pattern on the conversion element.

The light-conversion element converts at least part of the incident primary laser radiation into secondary light having a different spectral composition. It may comprise, for example, a luminescent or phosphorescent conversion material. The converted secondary light, optionally together with an unconverted portion of the primary light, forms a luminous image on or at the light-conversion element. The spectral characteristics of the resulting light may be selected to provide white light or another color suitable for vehicle illumination and signaling functions.

A projection system is arranged downstream of the light-conversion element. The projection system receives the luminous image generated at the conversion element and projects a corresponding image or light distribution into the area surrounding the vehicle, particularly onto the roadway ahead of or adjacent to the vehicle. The projection optics may include one or more lenses, mirrors, apertures, or other imaging elements configured to provide the required magnification, focus, orientation, and projection distance.

A control unit may operate the laser-light sources and microscanners in a coordinated manner according to stored image data, sensor information, vehicle operating conditions, or driver commands. In this way, the device can generate static or dynamic roadway patterns, such as illumination zones, lane-related markings, warning symbols, guidance information, or adaptive headlamp distributions. Individual laser sources may be switched, dimmed, or modulated independently, while the microscanners determine where the corresponding optical energy is deposited on the conversion element.

Transforming the intensity profile of each primary laser beam before scanning improves control over the formation of the luminous image. It can reduce unwanted intensity peaks, increase uniformity, enhance image contrast, and permit more efficient use of the available laser power. The combination of multiple independently conditioned beams, controlled microscanning, wavelength conversion, and projection optics therefore enables a compact and flexible vehicle-lighting device capable of producing a precisely defined roadway image.

## The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it is used before a noun when referring to a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “the book” suggests a particular book that is already known or has previously been mentioned.

Although it contains only three letters, “the” plays an important role in communication. It helps distinguish between something general and something specific. Compare “I saw a dog” with “I saw the dog.” The first sentence introduces an unspecified dog, while the second points to a particular one.

“The” can also identify unique things, such as the sun, the moon, or the Earth. It appears in geographical names like the Atlantic Ocean and the United Kingdom, as well as in titles such as *The Great Gatsby*.

Simple but essential, “the” brings precision and clarity to English. Its frequent use demonstrates how even the smallest words can have a significant influence on meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a vehicle laser lighting device with multiple laser sources, individual light guides, a phosphor conversion element, projection optics, and microscanners that direct beams with altered intensity profiles onto the conversion element.
counterfactuals.output: A vehicle laser lighting device includes a plurality of laser sources configured to emit respective laser beams, a plurality of light guides individually associated with the laser sources, and a phosphor conversion element configured to convert at least a portion of the laser radiation into wavelength-converted light. Projection optics project illumination generated by the phosphor conversion element into a vehicle environment. A plurality of microscanners are arranged to receive the laser beams from the respective light guides and to direct the beams onto selected regions of the phosphor conversion element. At least one beam is modified to have an intensity profile different from its initial intensity profile before or during scanning. Controlled operation of the laser sources and microscanners distributes laser energy over the conversion element to form a desired luminance distribution, reduce localized thermal loading, and generate a configurable projected light pattern.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for an automotive headlamp in one formal paragraph, describing at least two lasers whose beams travel through corresponding optical fibers, emerge with changed intensity distributions, scan a light-converting surface, and are projected onto the road.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to an automotive headlamp comprising at least two laser light sources configured to emit respective laser beams into corresponding optical fibers, through which the beams propagate and emerge with intensity distributions modified relative to their input distributions. A scanning device directs the emerging beams across a light-converting surface, such as a phosphor layer, which converts the incident laser light into illumination light. An optical projection system collects and projects the converted illumination light onto a roadway to produce a controlled vehicle lighting pattern.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise European-patent-style summary for a motor-vehicle lighting invention using two or more laser sources, beam-shaping light guides, microscanning elements, a wavelength converter, and projection optics that cast a luminous image onto the roadway.
counterfactuals.output: A motor-vehicle lighting device comprises at least two laser sources configured to emit respective laser beams, beam-shaping light guides arranged to homogenise and direct the laser beams, and microscanning elements configured to scan the shaped beams over a wavelength-converting element. The wavelength-converting element converts the scanned laser radiation into visible light defining a luminous image. Projection optics project the luminous image onto a roadway in front of the vehicle. A control unit may independently control the laser sources and microscanning elements to vary the intensity, distribution and/or position of the projected image, thereby providing an adaptive vehicle-lighting function.
